scope.note: Assets left Poly Network's LockProxy custody contracts on Ethereum, BSC and Polygon, released through each chain's cross-chain manager contract.

sources.quote: The hacker exploited the Proxy Lock Contracts of Poly Network on three different chains.
The exploit came from mismanagement of access rights between two vital Poly Network's smart contracts: EthCrossChainManager and EthCrossChainData.

sources.quote: On 10 August 2021, the Poly Network was attacked by a hacker, losing over $600 million.

amount_usd.range: 600.3M (Decrypt, 'at least') to 611M (DefiLlama, SoK, rekt.news); per chain: Ethereum 264.8M-272M, BSC 250M-250.8M, Polygon 85.09M

sources.quote: TOTAL VALUE LOST - ~$611,000,000
at least $600.3 million
Ten types of tokens — worth nearly $272 million — on the Ethereum blockchain have been stolen ... They transferred funds worth $250 million USD to BSC.

failure_class.phrase: Release-side cross-chain manager executed a message that replaced its keeper public key

sources.quote: The root cause of this exploit is that the EthCrossChainManager contract is allowed to change the Keepers.
The attacker accessed the function putCurEpochConPubKeyBytes(bytes) that updates the validators' public keys in the EthCrossChainData contract.
攻击原因是 Keeper 被攻击者篡改（而非私钥泄露）。

release_side.share_note: All value left LockProxy custody: Ethereum about 264.8M-272M USD (10 assets), BSC about 250M USD, Polygon about 85.09M USD (USDC only).

outflow.count_note: Counted: transactions moving assets out of a LockProxy to the recipient addresses, all three chains. Ethereum: 10 releases, one per asset, 09:51:02 (2,857.49 ETH) to 10:27:38 (616,082.59 FEI); in between USDC 96.39M at 09:55:44, WBTC 1,032.12 at 09:57:22, DAI 673,227.94 at 09:58:41, UNI 43,023.75 at 09:58:59, SHIB 259.7B at 10:03:50, renBTC 14.47 at 10:04:22, USDT 33.43M at 10:11:39, WETH 26,109.06 at 10:25:32 (Etherscan transaction pages; the DAI transaction was located from token logs, then read on Etherscan). Polygon: 2 releases, 85,089,610.91 USDC at 10:04:22 and 108.69 USDC at 10:29:21 (Polygonscan). BSC: 5 releases at 10:08:55, 10:09:37, 10:10:19, 10:10:58 and 10:28:35 (block timestamps of the BSC transactions listed by Merkle Science, read from a BSC RPC node on 2026-10-16 because BscScan refused automated reads). Keeper-key replacements preceded the releases on each chain: BSC 09:33:07, Ethereum 09:48:40, Polygon 10:04:14. Ethereum-only window 09:51:02-10:27:38 (36.6 min). Mudit Gupta dates the start to 09:33:07, which is the BSC key replacement, not a release.

pause.what: No time found for a Poly Network pause. Partners suspended dependent services on 2021-08-10: O3 Swap cross-chain function (X post status 1425079239162744842, 12:59:01Z), Neo Legacy to N3 migration, Flamingo, Switcheo. Poly Network restored cross-chain functionality for 59 assets on 2021-08-26, which implies its services had been suspended.
pause.by: unknown for Poly Network; partners suspended their own services
pause.note: One analysis notes the cross-chain manager was pausable; no source read says it was paused during the outflow.

limit_mechanism.how: No source mentions one; one analysis notes only that the manager contract was pausable. SoK Table 9 lists 'Set withdrawal limits' as a mitigation for this event.

returned.native: All assets: about 610M USD sent back by the recipient (the last 28,953 ETH and 1,032 WBTC through a shared multisig key) plus 33.43M USDT frozen by Tether and reissued to Poly Network
returned.note: Timeline: first return 2021-08-11 08:46 UTC (10,000 USDC on Polygon); 4.77M USD by a post at 7:47 a.m. ET on 08-11; about 256M USD by the end of 08-11; by 08-12 everything except the frozen USDT had been sent back, but about 141M USD sat in a 3-of-4 multisig that needed the recipient's key; 427M USD counted as returned on 08-19; key shared on-chain 2021-08-23 08:39:04 UTC and the remaining 141M USD retrieved; Tether issued 33.4M USDT to Poly Network's multisig on 2021-08-25. Tether froze the USDT on 08-10 (CTO post status 1425090760609832978, 13:44:48Z). Poly Network paid a 160 ETH bounty.

sources.quote: Seven minutes hence the hacker's Polygon address returned $10,000 in a stablecoin USDC to a wallet set up by Poly Network at 8:46 UTC.
So far, we have received a total value of $4,772,297.675 assets returned by the hacker.
The only funds the hacker hasn't returned are the $33 million in USDT that were frozen by Tether following the exploit.
assets worth approximately $427 million were returned by the hacker.
At 08:39:04 AM +UTC on August 23, 2021, Mr. White Hat publicly shared a private key
on August 25 Tether issued USDT totaling $33.4 million from tokens frozen after the protocol hack.

events.open_questions: Whether and when Poly Network paused its own manager or LockProxy contracts in August 2021 (a search for Paused events on the three managers would settle it). BSC release times rest on RPC block timestamps, not a published page. The per-asset split on BSC differs between rekt.news and Merkle Science. CertiK (search summary only, Medium page refused) puts the side-chain origin transaction at 09:32:32 UTC.

outflow.count_note: Counted: Bitcoin transactions from pNetwork's BTC custody paying the 100 recipient addresses listed in SoK reference 232. Two batch transactions, each with 100 outputs to the listed addresses: block 701295 at 17:35:24 UTC (100 x 1.38126597 = 138.13 BTC) and block 701297 at 17:42:08 UTC (100 x 1.37439399 = 137.44 BTC). An earlier single payment of 0.276 BTC to the first listed address in block 701293 at 17:22:03 UTC may be the one genuine peg-out request that the SoK mentions, or a first unauthorized payment; including it, the window is 17:22:03-17:42:08 (20.1 min, 3 transactions). The three payments total 275.84 BTC against 277 BTC reported. Times are Bitcoin block timestamps from mempool.space. The BSC-side transactions that emitted the events were not identified.

returned.note: pNetwork offered a 1.5M USD bounty (X post status 1439690598529765384, 20:39:21Z). The SoK states the funds still sat in the recipient addresses when it was written. pNetwork said it was working on a solution for pBTC-on-BSC holders (operator-side, kept separate).

scope.note: Funds left a BXH yield vault on BSC through its ControllerHub after the project's admin wallet granted a governance role to an outside contract. No bridge custody or mint is involved. The SoK describes it as a compromised key of a 'bridge smart contract on the destination chain'; the code walk-through by Fairyproof shows a vault and strategy structure instead. BXH calls itself a cross-chain exchange. DefiLlama has bridgeHack=false.

The private key associated with the bridge smart contract on the destination chain was compromised
a decentralized cross-chain cryptocurrency exchange program
At 3 o'clock on the 30th (UTC)
On October 29, 2021, the BXH (BOY X HIGHSPEED) cryptocurrency exchange experienced a hack of $139 million in tokens.
